notes: Version 2.4 corrects the status of the dimension, amplitude, phase-coherence, Born-weight and initial-transition statements and of the companion gravity and gauge results. The homogeneous dimension 4 follows from the Bass-Guivarc'h formula for the discrete Heisenberg group with two horizontal generators; the finite group has this growth only on balls of radius n << sqrt(q); it is a property of the supplied carrier and is not identified with the 3+1 structure of spacetime. Complex amplitudes are written on the supplied carriers (the Heisenberg-Schrodinger carrier and the spinor carrier of O23): coherence excludes a classical probability mixture but not real amplitudes, and real and quaternionic formulations are compared with their composition rules (Stueckelberg 1960, Renou et al. 2021, Barrios Hita et al. 2026, Adler 1995); a selection from the axioms is open. A3 forbids premature selection among open directions but does not by itself forbid an erasure of relative phases that selects no direction, so phase coherence is not derived from A3 alone; the WKB phase is an effective quantity on the supplied carrier. The comparison with holographic renormalisation states the conditions of Q6b: a supplied extension, a Newtonian exterior, the Schwarzschild form only with external dynamical input and no uniqueness. Phase invariance, positivity and normalisability do not single out the squared norm, so the Born weight is an additional rule; Gleason's theorem (1957) would need additivity over orthogonal decompositions, which is neither required nor derived, and dimension at least three. The abstract states the quantum-mechanical reading as the programme's thesis. Projective incompleteness does not guarantee the initial transition (Remark 4.11). The Einstein, Yang-Mills and Einstein-Yang-Mills statements of Gravity, Q12 and Q13 are stated with their hypotheses: a supplied metric and compact gauge group, couplings as matching data, a sufficient infrared condition, a Euclidean derivation; no coupling hierarchy is derived. Bibliography entries of cited corpus papers are synchronised with the programme registry. No Foundation theorem is changed.
